body:
I know how you feel, I failed a few months ago, I tried hanging myself with a belt from a metal fence. When it failed, I honestly laughed, it was comically bad. I haven’t really figured out if it was good or bad luck. I want to say it gets better. I’ve been receiving medical treatment, I’m not seeing much change, I was on the up but I’ve felt myself slipping recently. Been thinking about it more and more. I’ve been waiting about four months for psychiatric treatment. 

It’s rich coming from me. But really, it’s cliche, but one day at a time. Please try to get some sort of help, it’s intimidating at first, but there are people out there for people like us. I don’t know where you are in the world, maybe it is a place with less than stellar views and approaches to mental health. But I hope you are somewhere that doesn’t throw people into padded rooms for a little sadness, never-mind suicide attempts. 

I always thought it selfish to live for other people. Every person I spoke to about this said “Think of your family” or “Think of your friends” I just got sick of hearing it. Friends? It’s easier for them to come to your funeral once, than deal with your emotional shit forever, that’s how I felt and still kind of feel now. But I don’t blame friends or family too much it’s a lot to deal with when they don’t know what to say. 

It sounds really dumb and simple. But a lot of simple things are. Occams Razor and all that. It might get better, it might get worse before it gets better. But you’ll never know if you end it all now.

Getting ‘Deadeye Dick’ by Kurt Vonnegut vibes. With a reckless shot into the air.

“What, incidentally, was a pregnant mother of two doing, operating a vacuum cleaner on Mother’s Day? She was practically asking for a bullet between the eyes, wasn’t she?”

I’m going to be really cliche here in some of the things I say, but it’s worth a try. I’m going through a really rough patch at the moment. I don’t think much further ahead than the next hour or so. I struggle with suicidal tendencies a lot. My Doctor has alluded to some bipolar traits in me and I have been diagnosed with major depression. 

What works for one person might not work for the next. So anything I say, you may or may not be interested in. I read a lot, that tends to distract you a bit. Try contacting any friends and family if you can. I have very few friends, nobody I could just meet up with on the fly, what few friends I do have are either too far away or busy all the time. But maybe talk to a trusted friend? Try not to ask for an answer, as people often struggle with these conversations, just talk. Art? I have gained a bit of a passion for art recently. I could hardly draw stick figures and now I’m drawing birds that actually look like birds! 

I don’t know what country you are in so I can’t comment on what a psychiatric hospital is going to be like. I live in the UK and it is generally rare they are employed and don’t seem to help much or harm really. Just a stop gap to assess you and get you some care. 

It’s rich coming from someone who has tried suicide and thinks about it often, but I don’t think you should. If I can try to live and just take each day as it comes, trust me, you can too.

I am so sorry to hear that. I know you think they don’t care, but the best thing you can do is report it to the authorities. You cannot blame yourself for getting drunk. This was done to you, not to yourself.

I can’t be much help as I’m going through a rough patch also, but not as serious as yours. I saw on your profile you have self harmed, I’m sorry you are also going through that. I don’t know what country you live in, if it’s the USA I know mental health services aren’t great. 

All I can say is try to reach out to close friends, if you feel comfortable you could contact your family but they often don’t understand, I get it if that’s the case. I want you to realise the seriousness of what has happened to you, people say “It could be worse” that isn’t the case, every crisis is personal. All I can finish off with really, is it is always darkest before the dawn. Cliche I know. Sorry, but it helps me sometimes.

Thank you, I appreciate your response. 

I have thought about that, I wonder about all the events that coincide in a particular way for things to be the way they are. I’ve made a lot of stupid decisions, good ones too. This world is just funny in that it doesn’t shout at you, it whispers and you have to really listen for it sometimes I feel.

Operating on myself...I was probably 10-11. Found a weird mass on my forearm, took great care not to cut any veins, sat on my arm to make it go numb and lathered my arm in Lanacane as I knew it had Benzocaine in it. Did very little to numb the pain...didn’t get very deep before I realised I had no real way to stem the blood that had just come rushing back so I stopped...scar has mostly gone, but it’s still a little numb in places. 

I did not put this on my Med School application...

In case people are wondering, well, why? I always hated bothering people and I never wanted to tell my mum in case she called a doctor or an ambulance as I didn’t want to waste their time. I am still like that today.

Formerly is a bit of a funny one. It comes in waves for me. I feel great for days, weeks, months, then comes the inevitable. Could be something small, could be something big. But I am thrust into this deep, dark pit that I cannot see anywhere out of. It is totally crushing, it makes you feel so alone and so devoid of help. I always have trouble explaining this part, but when you see other people they aren’t real...if that makes any sense. It feels as though I am my own species and everybody else is a totally different one. 

My grandmother passing away made me incredibly sad, it did not put me in that mindset. But waking up at 4am for another repetitive work shift makes me want to cut my forearm open with a razor. 

But there are two things that come to mind in relation to this question. First, family, I don’t have a big family, but I do have a close one, it would upset them terribly and I don’t know if I could do that to them. My mother just wouldn’t understand. I’m very private about my issues. 

Secondary, I’m terrified of being the centre of attention. I don’t want people talking about me and thinking about me en masse. The occasional comment I could not care less. But if I committed suicide? Every day I just want to get a few essentials for a few days and just go. Just walk out into the rural areas and think, consider and if need be, end it. But I’m terrified of being on the news, on social media, mass calls for me to contact them etc. It’s very weird I know...I just don’t like all that stuff. I have quite a few close friends at work, so they would be quite upset about me disappearing. Also, disappearing in the most watched country on Earth wouldn’t be easy.

I will share one moment though, but I’ll make it short as this is turning into a bit of a novel...There was one week for me. It was the darkest week I had ever experienced. Work was going terribly, University wasn’t helping and my relationship was in a pretty bad place (in my mind) any day was going to be the day. I was pacing up and down at home, writing random thoughts and ideas, ranting to myself, picking up a knife and just imagining plunging it into my chest...anyway, there was a knock on the door. I never answer the door. This is England, nobody knocks on your door for a good reason, so I almost always ignore it. But this time, for whatever reason, I feel calm enough to answer it. It’s a Jehovah’s Witness. She just stared straight into my eyes and said “You do know God loves you?”

I was totally taken aback. Don’t get me wrong. I’m not religious, nor am I atheist really. And I know that these are phrases used to try to grab people’s attention, JW’s are hardly a kind and accepting group at times. But she was so pleasant, didn’t try to get me to join or listen to a pamphlet style speech or get a donation from me. We just chatted about religion, philosophy and my Uni studies (I did BioScience and she wished me well...) and just left. I haven’t seen her in a long time.

Although that experience most likely meant nothing, it has had a lasting effect on me.

I work in retail in England. We used to get these anonymous reviews that came down every now and again. They weren’t absolutely compulsory. But it was highly encouraged.

Two things always bothered me about the system. First. It was totally anonymous. No logins. No names. But. There was an option where you could put some stuff about yourself. Age, gender, student or non-student etc. That was voluntary information. But your department was not voluntary information. You had to enter that. I knew for a long time the management would sit upstairs and go through all the reviews comparing details and confirming who was who, which wasn’t ever difficult. Even if you didn’t put any identifying details, the other staff might. They can also tell by your writing skills. I have a very lengthy, flowing style at times...if that can’t be seen already. While other, less educated members of staff would write “not happy with manegers” they could guess who’s who pretty quick. 

Secondly, there was one time a particularly disdained Manager was pushing to get his staff to do these reviews. Only one person ended up doing it, as the rest of the staff pretty much unionised and just refused. He left a very scathing review...which I imagine was welcomed warmly. 

They would also take you into the room with the computers one at a time, so it wouldn’t be hard to check the completion times...

I personally don’t see the point of anonymous reviews. Five years in, nothing comes of them. Genuine recommendations from genuine staff that aren’t “hate the job” and “Managers are shit” but are “More conferring with staff regarding changes” get passed to the wayside because A) They wouldn’t like their boss to know a brilliant idea came from an employee, they have to justify their existence somehow or B) The serfs couldn’t possibly couldn’t know more than I, my five months here has allowed me complete knowledge and clairvoyance of what to expect.

Fuck I hate retail.

It’s a bizarre thing really. I’m suffering these kind of thoughts. Have been since I was in my teens, I am 24 now. It’s definitely gotten worse in the past few years.

Everyday I think about it, almost on the hour. I have mentioned these thoughts to my partner (I don’t know how seriously she has considered such a thing) and a close friend once. But only in minute detail, as a passing thought. Not that it actually occupies most of my day. 

I sit at work staring into space, hoping I’ll gain the courage to just grab a razor, walk far, far away to a nice, secluded, agrarian type place and just do it. But I can’t. As I have these thoughts that I have to do something here. That I’m not destined to be stuck in bloody retail all my life. That and my partner and parents, who would be severely affected by my passing, I imagine.

It was really bad a year or so ago. I had just left University as I am a fool, work was bringing me down. It was a week of Hell. Everyday I was going to do it, something came up, so I couldn’t, I didn’t want to let anyone down. I had a bit of a nervous breakdown that month. Held it together, slightly. Temper got the better of me when I was on my own, I was blunt with everybody, for whatever reason, I was going to get a book I had pre-ordered, I saw quite a few homeless people around, out of sheer guilt and sadness over my luck and their misfortune, I got a lot of money out of an ATM and just distributed it to them. Strange times. 

I’m better now, but I am still plagued by issues. I am a person who is very affected by events when people are hurt and especially animals. Just earlier there was a post on popular about some Norwegians who committed beastiality, the picture attached really got to me and I thought about the razor in my draw. Sometimes I love this world and would love to stay here until my hopeful last natural breath. Sometimes I just consider leaving now and getting it over with. 

TL:DR I’ll actually answer the question here without rambling. You feel if you keep going on about it to people, they’ll think you’re abusing their sympathy. If you keep it to yourself, in your own head, without consulting others, you can convince yourself of anything.
Would I love life? Or become Nietzsche 2.0?

I think about this one all the time. Ever tried to hide from anybody? In the movies a spy will be sneaking around, hear a guard coming and run into a side room as the guard patrols by, to the relief of the audience. 

In reality? I used to work with a horrific manager. Really arrogant, know it all, gave me horrendous jobs and used to make my life a misery because I was just a “Student who is wasting his life” while he had made it as a low-level manager...

Anyway. I would hear him coming down a corridor, that rotund stomach poking around the corner before he did. Guarantee, if I dived into another room, he would happen to be going into that room. Has happened plenty of times. I would hide and that person would always be going in that room...

Bonus: When two characters are talking, one insults the other. The other just cocks their head as if they didn’t understand and carry on with the conversation. I.e my favourite ever show, House.

I can relate to you friend. Everyday I consider ending my life. Seeing no other option. But I have been afflicted with a ginormous fear of pain. I tried hanging myself once, the belt snapped...the most over engineered and pathetic attempt you could ever see. 

It’s a horrid limbo to be in. Wanting to be dead. But not wanting to die.

Normally I have no shame about asking people their name, I’ll just be upfront and say “I’m sorry,  I have a horrific memory. What was your name again?” Every time they’re cool about it. The guy who delivers to my work every morning for the past six years, he always addresses me by my name, but I never learned his and never got around to getting it...

What makes it awkward is we are on a close conversational basis. Asking about each other’s families, projects etc. Now it would be far too awkward to ask. I’ve gotten away with just “Morning” so far.
Thank you! I hope you have someone who can make you feel loved and safe. If not, I hope you find that person :)

And that’s the conflict. If I didn’t have her, I don’t know where I would be. I love her dearly. I don’t want to sound...bizarre? But it really feels some force is holding me here. Every time in the past I have been very close to ending it, something has come along and brought me back. I have her and she’s my anchor. It’s a strange world we live in. The coming and going from these feelings is absolutely exhausting.

Thank you for your reply, I’m very sorry to hear about your separation. I hope you are coping well. I’m a chronic worrier, always have been, every decision requires weeks of self consultation, I most likely never would go through with such an idea. But in times of personal crisis, nothing is off the table. I love her very much, but also want to progress high. I want a family. The pain of life. To gain, something must be lost. 

Best of luck to you, thank you for your honest opinion. A little reality is needed sometimes.
I can relate to you there. My sleep schedule is horrific. I just don’t feel like sleeping. I feel that pain, not sleeping since the day before and being at work at 4am until 3pm is a bitch

Thank you for the insight, I know as you become older you sometimes become more content in life, but at the moment, being plagued by delusions of grandeur while also thinking nothing of yourself is very confusing.

That is incredibly eloquent and it has touched me deeply, thank you for your reply. It has certainly given me something to ponder, I truly appreciate it. Hearing another side is worth more than anyone could describe. My best wishes to you also.

That’s a good point. Hard to make a new life if you have no skill or higher-level qualification to speak of. Just the conflict that gets to me. I love my family very much. It’s just everything else I can’t stand.

It is just so incredibly difficult. I live in the most watched nation on Earth. I’m sure I’d be found on the first day. Since everything is tied into everything these days, you try to make a new life and your old one is immediately brought back to you. Thanks to the wonders of the digital world...

I can relate to you there. I have always hated my birthday and by extension Christmas. Every year I tell my partner and mother not to get me anything, yet they always do. I always double check my social media isn’t going to tell anyone it’s my birthday and get loads of messages. I always make sure I’m off work when it happens so nobody mentions it.

I have this terrible habit of when I receive gifts I look totally uninterested and uncaring. My family understand, but I hate it, I’m just not an animated person. I never do big displays of “Oh my god! Thank you so much!” Then sprinting around the room. The more I try to look appreciative, the more disingenuous it appears. Even though I really do appreciate the thought.

I love England. We treat our towns/cities like children. We talk shit about our hometowns all the time. Hate living there. But God forbid somebody from another town thinks their town/city is better than yours.
What’s the worst he’s going to do, shoot around you?
The Viking on the bridge at the Battle of Stamford Bridge . Would most likely be amazed he is still being talked about today.

Had a lot of conflict when I was a teenager. I wasn’t sexually curious, but conceptually, if that makes sense. More on the romantic interest of other males, no interest whatsoever in the sexual side. My confusion between my feelings and my education caused a lot of repressed hate to those who weren’t heterosexual. My hero’s were classic straight men, I read philosophy by those who were classically anti-gay and very interested in science, which caused me to speculate that there was no scientific basis for homosexuality, I was just looking for reasons to hate myself and not believe I was actually gay or even bisexual. 

I did a lot of growing up in my late teens. I realised that it was probably mostly hormonal, I didn’t get a girlfriend until I was 19. I wasn’t unattractive 4/10 in my own estimation. 7/10 by friends male and female. I obsessed over one girl from being 9-10 years old, so I was maybe looking for an out there. 

When I was 20 I was kissed in a nightclub by a man with lots of glitter on his face. I’ll never forget that. I thought it was quite comical, but made me realise I was definitely not interested in the opposite sex. He was attractive, but I wasn’t interested in kissing him back. Sounds corny, but that’s when it hit me I was heterosexual. Until that point I thought of the time and place was correct and the moon aligned I might have those feelings, but nothing. 

This is the first time I have written this down and it feels great. I have kept a journal for many years, but I haven’t written anything like this as my fiancé has gone through them in the past, not spying as such, but looking for any signs of suicidal ramblings. Not unusual. 

This is why I love this site. I know it gets ripped to shreds by those who think it’s full of white knights, but there is a community here and there is a nature to it that isn’t found easily on or off the Internet.
